preamble: Coda lenition turns a syllable-final voiceless alveolar stop [t] into the voiceless velar fricative [x]: the stop becomes a fricative and its coronal place is lost. Sakhalin Ainu is the documented case. Where Hokkaido Ainu keeps syllable-final /p/, /t/, /k/ and /r/, Sakhalin Ainu lenited these codas and merged them into a single phoneme /x/, written with small katakana h and transliterated h. Hokkaido set 'bed' and kut 'belt' correspond to Sakhalin seh and kuh. The change is confined to one dialect group of the Ainu family, so it is rare.

examples.from: Hokkaido (Ishikari) Ainu set 'bed, nest' (retains the stop)
examples.note: The Sakhalin form is from the Karafuto word list; the Hokkaido form from the Ishikari word list.
